A1.justification: Both PDFs contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices describing the same block-approximation work. Despite the changed title and method name, matching formulations, PCA visualizations, and retained classification results support a reliable comparison.

before.justification: v1 reports original representation analyses, classification experiments, and block-skipping comparisons in Section 4 and appendix Tables 5–7.

after.justification: v5 retains original empirical results and adds ImageNet, zero-shot classification, cross-dataset transfer, approximator comparisons, and misclassification analyses in Section 4 and Appendix A.2.

M1.justification: RBA is renamed TBA and retains the shared, closed-form least-squares linear replacement. v5 Section 3 explicitly extends replacement to multiple non-overlapping spans, tested through configurations such as 1→2, 4→5; v1 describes and evaluates individual spans. The fitting objective and basic replacement component remain unchanged.

E1.justification: v1 evaluates classification on MNIST, F-MNIST, CIFAR-10, and coarse/fine CIFAR-100. v5 retains these and adds ImageNet1k, OpenCLIP zero-shot classification, and transferring transformations between source and target datasets (Section 4.2; Tables 2–3 and 14–15). These substantially broaden the evaluated task conditions.

E2.justification: v5 adds trained MLP and Res-MLP approximators as evaluated alternatives on ImageNet1k (Table 5), substantially broadening comparison beyond the original model and block skipping. v1's Skip comparator is retained as SkipAt Identity, with largely identical scores; its renaming and attribution do not constitute a new comparator.

E3.justification: The primary similarity analysis changes from cosine similarity of CLS representations to MSE of mean-token representations. v5 also adds ViT-T/ViT-L configurations, disjoint-span tests, zero-shot and transfer procedures, and 300-step Adam training for nonlinear comparators. The existing 3,000-sample transformation fit and five-epoch linear-probe protocol are retained.

E4.justification: Beyond v1's skipping ablation and representation analyses, v5 adds comparisons of MSE, cosine similarity, and CKA (Figure 6), mean-token versus CLS analysis, transformation-complexity ablations, cross-dataset transfer analyses, and class-level errors, confusion matrices, and misclassified examples (Figures 12–14). Most earlier PCA panels are retained in Figures 7–11.

E5.justification: Both versions report three-seed classification experiments with ± summaries, and v5 retains this convention for expanded classification and approximator comparisons. No increased replication, new uncertainty estimator, confidence intervals, or significance tests are documented. Added zero-shot and transfer tables provide point estimates without an additional uncertainty procedure.

E6.justification: v5 adds substantial ImageNet, zero-shot, transfer, and approximator results and revises many retained scores. For ViT-S 7→10 on CIFAR-10, v1 Table 5 reports 85.81±1.03, whereas v5 Table 8 reports 87.36±0.17; v5 Table 4 still retains the earlier value. These are changed reports, with unexplained inconsistencies preventing a clean performance-gain interpretation.

T1.justification: The formal redundancy criterion broadens from adjacent-block BR(b) in v1 Equation (1) to MSE over arbitrary endpoint pairs (s,e) in v5 Section 3, which also specifies a non-overlap condition for composing replacements. This is a limited formal generalization; the least-squares formulation remains unchanged, and neither version supplies proofs or guarantees.

C1.justification: v5 withdraws the contribution claim of introducing a new BR metric, instead presenting MSE as an existing sufficient measure. It focuses the framework on vision transformers and makes cross-dataset generalization and effectiveness relative to trained approximators explicit headline claims. The central claim of efficient linear block replacement is retained.

C2.justification: v5 adds interpretations of poor MNIST-source transfer, compatibility with different similarity metrics and token summaries, and class-specific vulnerabilities. Appendix A.2.6 introduces a regularization explanation for late DEiT-S approximation. It also discusses large-model hardware limitations and redirects future work toward finer block granularity and token types, replacing v1's emphasis on topological metrics.

D1.justification: v1 lists model identifiers and software and promises a future implementation. v5 adds approximator architectures and code listings, their training budget, the 500-sample similarity-analysis subset, additional model identifiers, and GPU hardware details. It states that a supplementary code ZIP is provided; the archive itself is not included in the supplied PDFs for verification.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially expands efficiency positioning through residual-block ensembles, dynamic routing, data-free compression, second-order pruning, SkipAt, and few-sample transformer compression. It recognizes that some CNN compression avoids further training and explicitly attributes the skipping comparison to SkipAt. The BR novelty claim is also replaced by positioning MSE as an existing tool.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, and conclusion are extensively rewritten, with RBA/BR terminology replaced by TBA/MSE. The experimental narrative merges the earlier latent-analysis sections and separates performance from comparisons. Limitations become a dedicated section, and the appendix is reorganized into descriptive implementation and analysis subsections.

P2.justification: v5 redesigns similarity heatmaps and block-sensitivity plots, consolidates the main PCA comparison, and relocates retained PCA panels to the appendix. Classification tables are reorganized around parameter reductions and relative accuracy changes. New comparison, transfer, and error-analysis displays, code listings, and highlighted takeaway boxes substantially change the presentation.

improvement.justification: v1's validation largely relied on small-dataset classification and skipping comparisons. v5's ImageNet, zero-shot, transfer, nonlinear-approximator, and error analyses substantially strengthen assessment of generality, design choices, and failure conditions, alongside better reproducibility documentation. Reporting problems remain: scores and parameter counts conflict across tables, and Table 1 prints a 27.74% DiNO-B 9→11 ImageNet drop although its accuracies imply 37.39%. These weaken quantitative precision but do not outweigh the substantially stronger empirical basis.
